translations.idiomatic: Mi had always won men's hearts; many who wept vomited blood.

sentences.zh: 邴元真之降也，世充以為行臺仆射，鎮滑州。

translations.literal: When Bing Yuanzhen surrendered, Shichong made him Vice Director of the Great Headquarters and garrisoned Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing Yuanzhen surrendered, Shichong made him Vice Director of the Great Headquarters and garrisoned Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 密故將杜才幹恨其背密，偽以兵歸之，斬取其首，祭密冢，已乃歸國。

translations.literal: Mi's former officer Du Caigan hated him for betraying Mi; he falsely returned with troops, beheaded him and took his head, sacrificed it at Mi's tomb, and then returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's former officer Du Caigan hated him for betraying Mi. He falsely returned with troops, beheaded him and took his head, sacrificed it at Mi's tomb, and then returned to the state.

sentences.zh: 附單雄信單雄信，曹州濟陰人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Shan Xiongxin. Shan Xiongxin was a man of Jiyin in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Shan Xiongxin. Shan Xiongxin was a man of Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 與翟讓友善。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Zhai Rang.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Zhai Rang.

sentences.zh: 能馬上用槍，密軍中號「飛將」。

translations.literal: He could use a spear on horseback; in Mi's army he was called the "Flying General."
translations.idiomatic: He could use a spear on horseback. In Mi's army he was called the "Flying General."

sentences.zh: 偃師敗，降世充，為大將。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Yanshi he surrendered to Shichong and became a great general.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Yanshi he surrendered to Shichong and became a great general.

sentences.zh: 秦王圍東都，雄信拒戰，槍幾及王，徐世勣呵之曰：「秦王也！」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin besieged the Eastern Capital, Xiongxin resisted in battle; his spear nearly reached the prince. Xu Shiji shouted: "That is the Prince of Qin!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin besieged the Eastern Capital, Xiongxin resisted in battle. His spear nearly reached the prince. Xu Shiji shouted, "That is the Prince of Qin!"

sentences.zh: 遂退。

translations.literal: He thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後東都平，斬洛渚上。

translations.literal: Afterward when the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was beheaded on the Luo ford.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward when the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was beheaded on the Luo ford.

sentences.zh: 附祖君彥祖君彥，齊仆射孝徵子。

translations.literal: Appendix: Zu Junyan. Zu Junyan was the son of Qi Minister over the Masses Xiaozheng.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zu Junyan. Zu Junyan was the son of Qi Minister over the Masses Xiaozheng.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，屬辭贍速。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned with a strong memory and composed prose swiftly and abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned with a strong memory and composed prose swiftly and abundantly.

sentences.zh: 薛道衡嘗薦之隋文帝，帝曰：「是非殺斛律明月人兒邪？

translations.literal: Xue Daheng once recommended him to Emperor Wen of Sui. The emperor said: "Is this not the son of the man who killed Hulü Mingyue?
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daheng once recommended him to Emperor Wen of Sui. The emperor said, "Is this not the son of the man who killed Hulü Mingyue?

sentences.zh: 朕無用之。」

translations.literal: I have no use for him.
translations.idiomatic: I have no use for him."

sentences.zh: 煬帝立，尤忌知名士，遂調東都書佐，檢校宿城令，世謂祖宿城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne he especially feared famous scholars and therefore transferred him to Eastern Capital clerk, Inspector of Suicheng Magistrate—the world called him Zu of Suicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne he especially feared famous scholars and therefore transferred him to Eastern Capital clerk and Inspector of Suicheng Magistrate—the world called him Zu of Suicheng.

sentences.zh: 負其才，常郁郁思亂。

translations.literal: Trusting in his talent, he was often depressed and contemplated rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in his talent, he was often depressed and contemplated rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及為密草檄，乃深斥主闕。

translations.literal: When he drafted proclamations for Mi, he deeply denounced the sovereign's faults.
translations.idiomatic: When he drafted proclamations for Mi, he deeply denounced the sovereign's faults.

sentences.zh: 密敗，世充見之，曰：「汝為賊罵國足未？」

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, Shichong saw him and said: "Have you cursed the state enough as a bandit?"
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was defeated, Shichong saw him and said, "Have you cursed the state enough as a bandit?"

sentences.zh: 君彥曰：「跖客可使刺由，但愧不至耳！」

translations.literal: Junyan said: "Zhi's guest could be made to assassinate You—but I regret I did not reach that far!"
translations.idiomatic: Junyan said, "Zhi's guest could be made to assassinate You—but I regret I did not reach that far!"

sentences.zh: 世充令撲之。

translations.literal: Shichong ordered him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong ordered him beaten.

sentences.zh: 既困臥樹下，世充已自欲盜隋，中悔，命醫許惠照往視之，欲其蘇。

translations.literal: When he was exhausted and lay beneath a tree, Shichong himself already wished to usurp the Sui and halfway regretted it; he ordered the physician Xu Huizhao to go examine him, wishing him to revive.
translations.idiomatic: When he was exhausted and lay beneath a tree, Shichong himself already wished to usurp the Sui and halfway regretted it. He ordered the physician Xu Huizhao to go examine him, wishing him to revive.

sentences.zh: 郎將王拔柱曰：「弄筆生有余罪。」

translations.literal: Commander Wang Bazhu said: "The man who wields the brush has more than enough guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wang Bazhu said, "The man who wields the brush has more than enough guilt."

sentences.zh: 乃蹙其心，即死，戮屍於偃師。

translations.literal: He then pierced his heart, and he died at once. The corpse was exposed at Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: He then pierced his heart, and Junyan died at once. The corpse was exposed at Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 【贊】贊曰：或稱密似項羽，非也。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The commentary says: Some call Mi similar to Xiang Yu—but it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The commentary says: Some call Mi similar to Xiang Yu—but it is not so.

sentences.zh: 羽興五年霸天下，密連兵數十百戰不能取東都。

translations.literal: Yu rose in five years and dominated the realm; Mi fought in succession for dozens and hundreds of battles yet could not take the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yu rose in five years and dominated the realm. Mi fought in succession for dozens and hundreds of battles yet could not take the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 始玄感亂，密首勸取關中；

translations.literal: At the start when Xuangan rebelled, Mi first counseled taking Guanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: At the start when Xuangan rebelled, Mi first counseled taking Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 及自立，亦不能鼓而西，宜其亡也。

translations.literal: when he established himself he likewise could not beat the drums and go west—it was fitting that he perished.
translations.idiomatic: When he established himself he likewise could not beat the drums and go west—it was fitting that he perished.

sentences.zh: 然禮賢得士，乃田橫徒歟，賢陳涉遠矣！

translations.literal: Yet in honoring the worthy and winning men he was like Tian Heng and his followers; how far he surpassed Chen She!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in honoring the worthy and winning men he was like Tian Heng and his followers. How far he surpassed Chen She!

sentences.zh: 噫，使密不為叛，其才雄亦不可容於時雲。

translations.literal: Alas—if Mi had not rebelled, his heroic talent likewise could not have been tolerated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—if Mi had not rebelled, his heroic talent likewise could not have been tolerated in his time.
